Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis (initial impression): Bell’s palsy suspected; need formal neurological examination to confirm and to assess for alternative etiologies
  - Rationale: Unilateral facial numbness on the left side with hearing changes; clinician mentioned Bell’s palsy as a possible diagnosis and recommended in-person neurological exam and ENT ear examination to confirm

- Differential diagnoses supported/refined by DDx content:
  - Acoustic schwannoma / vestibular schwannoma (vestibular schwannoma)
    - Likelihood: Medium-High
    - Justification: Unilateral sensorineural hearing loss with tinnitus and dizziness; left-sided symptoms; family history of neurofibromatosis raises concern for NF2-associated tumors; no fever or ear discharge
  - Labyrinthitis / vestibular neuritis
    - Likelihood: Medium
    - Justification: Unilateral hearing loss with tinnitus and episodic dizziness; prior labyrinthitis history supports inner ear inflammatory pathology; duration weeks rather than acute
  - Bell’s palsy (idiopathic facial nerve palsy)
    - Likelihood: Medium
    - Justification: Unilateral facial numbness around the ear/jaw; clinician raised this possibility; typical Bell’s palsy involves facial weakness (not described here), but early presentations can be variable
- Considerations:
  - Vertebrobasilar insufficiency / posterior circulation ischemia (Low)
  - Other rare etiologies (e.g., CPA/multifocal lesions) may account for similar symptoms; no focal motor or visual deficits described yet

- Plan actions:
  - In-person face-to-face neurological examination today to assess facial nerve function and cranial nerves, and to perform a formal neuro exam
  - ENT/ear evaluation to inspect the ear and assess for local pathology
  - In Central London, arrange an in-clinic appointment with a GP to facilitate neurological assessment and imaging considerations as indicated
  - Provide patient support contact and facilitate prompt scheduling today
  - Consider audiology evaluation and vestibular assessment as part of further work-up
